message.content:
Since \(BQ\) and \(BP\) are the two trisectors of angle \(B\), they divide \(\angle B\) into three equal parts. Thus

\[
\angle QBP=\frac{\angle B}{3}=14^\circ
\]

so

\[
\angle B=42^\circ.
\]

Given \(\angle A=39^\circ\), we get

\[
\angle C=180^\circ-39^\circ-42^\circ=99^\circ.
\]

At \(C\), the trisector \(CP\) gives

\[
\angle BCP=\frac{\angle C}{3}=\frac{99^\circ}{3}=33^\circ.
\]

In triangle \(BPC\),

\[
\angle PBC=14^\circ,\qquad \angle BCP=33^\circ.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\angle BPC=180^\circ-14^\circ-33^\circ=133^\circ.
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{133}\).
